To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the correlation between Ebola search volumes and voting for Republican candidates is not statistically significant after accounting for time series autocorrelation and (b) the correlation between Republican support and the bandwagon effect is not statistically significant.

1) The correlation between Ebola search volume and support for Republican candidates in the 2016 elections is spurious and can be explained by the existence of temporal autocorrelation in both time series; 2) There was no correlation between Ebola search volumes and Republican voting in the 2012 elections; 3) There was no association between the number of Ebola infections and Republican voting in any of the elections we examined.
